Scalers to mid-caps: crossings into mid-cap status

Source: R/compute-midcap.R
compute_midcap_transitions.Rd

New analysis. Follows firms from the start of the 3-year window that first makes them a scaler (or a non-scaler of the pool) and records when they cross into mid-cap status, with firm exit as a competing event.

Usage

compute_midcap_transitions(
  config,
  accounts_indicators,
  money_unit = c("EUR thousand", "EUR"),
  top_cutoffs = c(top50 = 50, p1 = 0.01, p5 = 0.05, p10 = 0.1, p25 = 0.25)
)

Arguments

config

A scaleup_config from config_scaleup().

accounts_indicators

The output of build_accounts_indicators(); needs employment, and for the first two definitions turnover and total_assets.

money_unit

Unit of turnover and total_assets in accounts_indicators: "EUR thousand" (what build_accounts_indicators() produces, see financials_unit in config_scaleup()) or "EUR" (for an indicators panel built in euros by an earlier version of the package). As a check, the function stops if firms with 10-49 employees have a median turnover per employee above 5,000 when "EUR thousand" is declared (EUR 5 m per person: euros, not thousands).

top_cutoffs

Cut-offs of compute_top_scalers(): each top-scaler sample (e.g. HGE20_rel_p10) is also followed, from t-3 of its first year in the sample, category ALL only, so its crossings compare with those of all scalers (the link between the two analyses). NULL skips them.

Value

A list of tibbles:

  • incidence: by definition, sample, category, group (at entry) and step: firms at risk, crossings to mid and to large, exits, censored, and the cumulative incidence of each (Aalen-Johansen);

  • entry: per definition, sample, category and group, the firms entering the risk set and those not followed, by reason;

  • by_year: per definition, sample, category, group and calendar year, firms at risk, crossings, exits and status_missing: at-risk firm-years without a status (no row that year, or values that cannot decide it), where a crossing could neither start nor be confirmed;

  • coverage: per year, firm-years with 100+ employees and how many of them have both turnover and total assets (the financial coverage behind the first two definitions);

  • hazard: discrete-time logit of a crossing (to mid or large) in year t, one per definition and scaler type, on scalers and their pool non-scalers together (scaler = 1 for the scalers' spells). Covariates at t-1: log employment, 1-year employment growth, log turnover per employee and, where present, independence and exporter status; plus a young-firm dummy (age class 0-5 at t-1), years since entry and its square, and a linear calendar trend. Firm-clustered standard errors (CR1); ame_scaler is the average change in the yearly crossing probability when scaler goes from 0 to 1. Exits count as no crossing in their year (a cause-specific hazard). Two models each (window): from_t-3, every step; after_window, only the years after the growth window (step 4 = t + 1 on) of firms that had not crossed by t, so the scaler effect is net of the growth that defines a scaler.

Details

Status per firm-year, three definitions (definition column):

  • small_midcap: EU small mid-cap (Recommendation (EU) 2025/1099). A firm leaves the SME category (Recommendation 2003/361/EC) with 250+ persons, or with turnover above EUR 50 m and balance sheet above EUR 43 m. It is a small mid-cap if it then has fewer than 750 persons and turnover of at most EUR 150 m or a balance sheet of at most EUR 129 m; above those ceilings it is large.

  • sme_exit: leaving the SME category; large from 3,000 employees (the EIB mid-cap bound).

  • employment_250: 250+ employees; large from 3,000 employees. The reference series (no balance sheet, no inflation).

Money in EUR thousand, nominal (thresholds 50,000 / 43,000 / 150,000 / 129,000); balance sheet = total_assets. Firm-level figures (the legal definition adds up linked enterprises; use the independent breakdown). Nothing is imputed: a status is missing when the available values cannot decide it (e.g. turnover above EUR 50 m, under 250 employees, no balance sheet). Where consolidation_code exists, only unconsolidated accounts (U1, U2) get a status.

Crossing. The first year after entry into the risk set in which the firm is above SME status (mid or large) and is so again in the next calendar year. A missing year or an exit before the confirmation year is not a crossing. The crossing's type is the status in the crossing year: mid or large (the firm jumped past the mid-cap band).

Risk set. A firm's sample year t is its first year as a scaler (HGE20 / HGT20), as a non-scaler of the pool (HGE20_nonscaler_pool / HGT20_nonscaler_pool, as in compute_characteristics(); firms that scale later stay in it) or as a top scaler (see top_cutoffs), with 10 to fewer than 250 employees at t-3, from the fourth panel year. The firm enters the risk set at t-3, the start of that growth window, so a crossing during the growth spell itself counts. Scalers and pool firms are both observed at t-3 and t, so both groups survive the first three steps by construction. Entry needs SME status at t-3: firms already above it, or without a status, are counted (n_above_at_entry, n_status_missing_at_entry) and not followed. Breakdowns are the categories at t-3 (L3size_cat, L3age_cat, ...).

Time is years since entry (step 1 = t-2). A firm that crosses at step k has its event at k; a firm whose last year L is before the panel's last year exits at step L - entry (competing event); other firms are censored at the last step whose crossing could still be confirmed (panel end - 1 - entry). Firms with no step left are counted (n_no_followup).
